scenes.speaker: mott
lines: In 1947, a moth made a computer fail.

scenes.speaker: mott
lines: Like me. Picture Harvard, 1947. The Mark II.

scenes.speaker: mott
lines: A room full of relays: little metal switches that click open and shut to do math.

scenes.speaker: mott
lines: On September 9th, it started making errors. So the team went looking for the problem…

scenes.speaker: mott
lines: and found her. A moth, stuck between the contacts.

scenes.speaker: mott
lines: So they did the most engineer thing ever. They taped her into the logbook, and wrote:

scenes.speaker: mott
lines: "First actual case of bug being found."

scenes.speaker: mott
lines: Nope. Engineers already called glitches bugs. Edison wrote it in 1878.

scenes.speaker: mott
lines: That's the joke. An actual bug.

scenes.speaker: leo
lines: And Grace Hopper found it, right?

scenes.speaker: mott
lines: Bright light. Lamp or fire? She was on the team, and she helped make the story famous.

scenes.speaker: mott
lines: That page is still kept at the Smithsonian. Moth included.

scenes.speaker: leo
lines: So every time I debug something…

scenes.speaker: mott
lines: …you're talking about my family. Stay curious. Not too close to the light.
